results.title: Mechanisation
results.creator_credit: Michael Latham, Antony Jay, Peter Robinson and Video Arts
results.brief_description: Uses animation and documentary footage to show that as well as specialisation, another way of creating more wealth with the same number of people is through mechanisation. Shows that mechanisation has two forms: (i) finding more energy and (ii) using the energy you already have more efficiently and productively.

results.title: Mont Blanc: the fool killer
results.brief_description: Mont Blanc at 15,781 feet is the highest mountain in Europe and a graveyard to many reckless climbers. Frederick Burlingham, the director/photographer of this film, has scaled Mont Blanc four times. This film shows close-ups of Mont Blanc through the eyes of a telescope, focusing on some of the areas where many mountaineers have perished. Includes footage of Aiguille de Midi, a precipitous needle of 12,606 feet and a climbing party on some very tall crags. Interesting film from a historical point of view, notably the way the climbing party are dressed and how they are just roped together - very different from today’s climbers!

results.title: Mecca: the forbidden city
results.brief_description: The world’s 600 million Muslims are expected to make the pilgrimage to Mecca at least once in their lives. The film traces the ritual of the progress from Medina to Mecca, during which various rites are performed at the stopping places. A glimpse is given of the catering arrangements for 1,500,000 people, mostly men. The pilgrims enter the great Mosque where the sacred Ka’aba stands, centre of their devotions.

results.title: Monsters, Inc. [DVD]
results.creator_credit: Peter Docter, Darla Anderson, Disney and Pixar Animation Studios
results.brief_description: From the crew at Pixar (Toy story, A Bug’s life) comes “Monsters Inc.”, a story set amidst the world of monsters. The set-up is simple: at Monsters Incorporated, the staff (a delightfully bizarre looking myriad of creatures) work hard at eliciting screams from scared children, which are then bottled and used to power Monstropolis, the city where the monsters live. Sully, the top scarer at Monster’s Inc., gets into strife one night when he accidentally lets a child (a dangerous and toxic being in the monster world) over to the other side of her bedroom door. Sully and Mike (his best buddy) struggle to get Boo safely back to her bedroom, and keep her from the clutches of the CDA (Child Detection Agency). Of all the feature length films made by Pixar, this is the first to be set in a fictional world, which allows the animators a limitless palette in which to flex their imagination. The computer animation of “Monsters Inc.” is superb and the humour consistent throughout. One of the finest sequences of the film is a ride through a cavernous chamber, with Boo, Mike and Sully jumping from door to door through various countries, in search of Boo’s bedroom.

results.title: Impact of mining
results.creator_credit: David Roberts, Don Murray and Film Australia
results.brief_description:
Episode of Series “Alligator Rivers Region”.
The second film in a series looking at the work of the Supervising Scientist following the Fox Report on Uranium mining in the Kakadu National Park region of the Northern Territory. To monitor possible problems, scientific studies were carried out before work began. Shows some of the field work and by the use of interviews examines possible problems which could occur.

results.title: Measuring matter: Volume 2
results.creator_credit: Bill Walker, Peter Dallas and Bill Walker Productions
results.brief_description: This entertaining video which uses an animated investigator Al the Alligator to explain questions of physics. Part one ‘Volume’ sees Al investigating the “Case of the mysterious Puddle of Water: to explain that volume means the space that matter takes up. Part two has Al investigating the “Case of the Falling Picture” where he discovers the effect that temperature has on solids, and liquids, eg. that ice becomes water or steam depending on the temperature. Suitable for Primary level students.

results.title: Measure of care: Alligator Rivers region
results.creator_credit: David Roberts, Don Murray and Film Australia
results.brief_description:
Episode of Series “Alligator Rivers Region”.
Following an environmental impact study by Mr Justice Fox, the Australian Government set up the Office of the Supervising Scientist to carry out scientific research in the Alligator River region of Kakadu National Park to establish base-line figures which would enable scientists to monitor the mining activities. This documentary deals in some detail with this research, and discusses the problems associated with mining in such an unusual and beautiful part of Kakadu National Park. Narrated by Robyn Williams.

results.title: Measuring matter: Volume 1
results.creator_credit: Bill Walker, Peter Dallas and Bill Walker Productions
results.brief_description: This entertaining video which uses an animated investigator Al the Alligator to explain questions of physics. Part one ‘Length’ sees Al investigating the “The Case of the missing running shoe” to solve the mystery of length, using only a metre stick. Part two ‘Mass’ has Al investigating what mass is. He learns to measure Mass and Matter using a tool for this, a balance. He learns that matter has mass and weight, but weight may change depending on the location of the matter. Suitable for Primary level students.
